sources.entry: soundfile - An audio library for reading and writing sound files, based on libsndfile, CFFI, and NumPy.

summary.one_liner: python-soundfile is a Python library for reading and writing audio files, wrapping libsndfile through CFFI and returning data as NumPy arrays.
summary.what_it_does: Reads and writes sound files through the libsndfile C library, accessed via CFFI. Audio data is represented as NumPy arrays. The main functions are read() and write() for whole files, and blocks() for reading short, optionally overlapping chunks, such as computing RMS level per block. The SoundFile class keeps a file open for step-by-step reading and writing, with seek, tell, truncate, and flush methods, and supports a context manager. It can also use virtual I/O and the buffer_read and buffer_write methods that bypass NumPy. The README says it opens all formats libsndfile supports, for example WAV, FLAC, OGG and MAT, with known issues writing OGG files.
use_cases: reading WAV files into NumPy arrays
converting audio between formats such as WAV to FLAC
processing long audio files in blocks
computing signal level or features per audio block
reading and writing sound files from Python scripts
notable: Wraps libsndfile, so it reads and writes many formats including WAV, FLAC, OGG and MAT
pip wheels on Windows, macOS and Linux bundle libsndfile
blocks() reads audio in overlapping chunks for block processing
SoundFile objects support explicit file handling and seeking
Thread-safe for concurrent reads through separate handles, but not for shared writers
caveats: Writing OGG files can produce empty files with certain libsndfile versions (issue #130)
Source installs require installing libsndfile separately through the system package manager
Dropped support for Python 3.9 and earlier in version 0.14.0
